section.sectionSummaryBrief: The preparation for the Giving of the Torah is the Counting of the Omer, which involves the refinement of the midos, and the power for this refinement comes from the aspect of "the morrow of the Shabbos," which is the essential pleasure.
section.t: Now, the preparation for the Giving of the Torah is the matter of the Counting of the Omer.
For,
the Counting of the Omer is the matter of the refinements,
and about this it is said, "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos,"
for "the morrow of the Shabbos" is above the level of Shabbos,
and this means,
that Shabbos
(mentioned here)
is the level of rest that follows exertion,
and "the morrow of the Shabbos" is the level of essential rest,
which is the level of the essence of pleasure.
And from this level is drawn the empowerment for the work of refinement.
And this is analogous to what was explained above regarding the matter of performing work,
that the performance of work is due to the pleasure one has in the thing,
because of which he descends with his power of action and his other faculties to do the work.
And similarly, it will be understood above,
that the power for the descent in the work of refinement is from the aspect of "the morrow of the Shabbos,"
the essence of pleasure.
And this is [the meaning of] "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos,"
that from the aspect of "the morrow of the Shabbos" the empowerment for the work of refinement of the Counting of the Omer is drawn,
for the explanation of "and you shall count" is as explained by the Alter Rebbe,
from the term "luminosity and clarity,"
that one must refine all the midos and make them such that they are luminous and clear.
And through this, afterwards, on the Festival of Shavuos, the aspect of the returning encompassing light is drawn,
about which it is said, "Until the morrow of the seventh Shabbos you shall count fifty days,"
which is the revelation of the aspect of the non-sensed pleasure.
For the main revelation of this will be in the future, on the day that is entirely Shabbos and rest,
and a semblance of this also shines during the third meal of Shabbos, as mentioned above.
And also on the day of Shabbos itself and on Shabbos eve, a semblance of this level shines,
therefore we then recite "A Psalm, a Song for the Shabbos Day,"
the day that is entirely Shabbos and rest.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Exodus from Egypt also contained the aspect of essential rest in a concealed manner, and this power enabled the Counting of the Omer, which itself requires completeness and perfection, reflecting that essential rest.
section.t: And it can be said,
that this [idea] that the Exodus from Egypt was a preparation for the Giving of the Torah—
[and] a preparation must be of the same kind as that which is being prepared for—
is because in the Exodus from Egypt there was also
(in concealment)
the aspect of essential rest,
the essence of light.
And this is what is stated,
"When you bring the people out of Egypt, you shall serve G-d on this mountain,"
for even in the Exodus from Egypt there was the matter that shone at the Giving of the Torah,
except that in the Exodus from Egypt it was in concealment,
and at the Giving of the Torah it was drawn forth in revelation.
And this is [the meaning of] "And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos,"
that this [fact] that the Exodus from Egypt is also called "the morrow of the Shabbos"
is because in the Exodus from Egypt there was also the essence of light,
the aspect of essential rest,
except that what was drawn forth then in revelation was for the sake of the Plague of the Firstborn,
rest after the war,
but in concealment there was also in this the aspect of essential rest.
And to add,
since from the matter of "the morrow of the Shabbos" that was in the Exodus from Egypt the empowerment for the Counting of the Omer is drawn—
"And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos"—
therefore,
there is an analogue of this matter also in the Counting of the Omer.
For,
regarding the Counting of the Omer it is said, "Seven complete weeks shall there be,"
that each count must be complete,
therefore if one omitted to count once, then [the count] is lacking for all the days of the counting,
because each one must be in completeness,
and moreover,
each one must be in perfection
[for the true meaning of completeness is
(not only that there is no lack in it,
but rather)
also the matter of perfection,
according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov
on the verse,
"The Torah of the L-rd is complete"—"and it is perfect,"
as explained above.
And based on this, it can be said,
that this [requirement] that each count must be complete
is
(not only that there should be no lack,
but rather)
that there should also be perfection in it],
and the matter of completeness and perfection is essential rest.
And through this, it is drawn forth afterwards to be "the morrow of the seventh Shabbos,"
the revelation of the essential pleasure,
at the time of the Giving of the Torah.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: At the Giving of the Torah, the essential delights of Atzmus were drawn forth, and similarly in the future redemption there will be the revelation of the essential rest, culminating in the day that is entirely Shabbos.
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "And I was by Him as a nursling, and I was His delight,"
that at the Giving of the Torah there was the drawing forth of the essential delights,
for this is "I am the L-rd your G-d,"
"I am that I am,"
which is not hinted at by any letter or any crownlet,
meaning,
that at the Giving of the Torah there was the drawing forth of the Awtsmoos.
But initially, there needed to be the Exodus from Egypt and the Counting of the Omer,
and after this preparation came the revelation of the Giving of the Torah,
the non-sensed pleasure,
the aspect of essential rest.
And likewise, it will also be in the future redemption,
for Mashiach is a man of peace,
the aspect of essential rest.
However, within the time of the future itself, there will be several levels,
as per the statement of our sages,
"A feast
(a meal)
the Holy One, blessed be He, will make for His righteous servants,"
which is analogous to rest after war,
sensed pleasure,
and afterwards there will be the day that is entirely Shabbos and rest,
non-sensed pleasure.
And then the intention of creation and the ultimate purpose of the Giving of the Torah will be completed,
[fulfilling] "And the glory of the L-rd shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see,"
[so that] "the L-rd will be One and His Name will be One,"
as He is written, so He is called.
